title: Understanding Quantum Superposition
text:
Quantum superposition dictates that a particle, prior to measurement, does not exist in a single defined state but rather in a weighted combination of all its possible states simultaneously. This principle fundamentally challenges classical Newtonian physics, suggesting that reality at the subatomic level is inherently probabilistic rather than deterministic.

The act of observation or measurement forces the quantum system to 'collapse' from this superposition into one definite, observable state. This collapse mechanism is central to many interpretations of quantum mechanics, including the Copenhagen interpretation. Research continues to explore how environmental decoherence influences this transition, offering deeper insights into the relationship between observer and observed reality.
